overview: A single-page Department of State cross-reference sheet filed under Japanese manufacturing, directing researchers to file 800.20294/2 for a March 23, 1936 communication from Tokyo concerning proposed Japanese legislation to prevent the disclosure of commercial information about Japanese factories.

people.name: Garrels
people.role: Sender or reporting officer in Tokyo; precise position not stated

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on proposed Japanese factory-secrecy law
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to another file containing a communication about proposed Japanese legislation against divulging commercial information on Japanese factories.
subfiles.summary: This filing note points to document 800.20294/2, identified with the number 1225. The referenced communication originated in Tokyo from Garrels on March 23, 1936, and concerned a proposed Japanese law intended to prevent disclosure of commercial information about Japanese factories. The underlying communication itself is not included on this page.

interest: The sheet is useful primarily as a provenance and discovery aid: it documents that reporting on proposed Japanese industrial-secrecy legislation existed but was filed elsewhere, apparently under 800.20294/2 rather than solely under the manufacturing classification 894.65. For historians, it highlights both Japanese concern with protecting factory information in 1936 and the State Department’s cross-classification practices, which can otherwise obscure related records.
